data.narrative:
Avalanche Energy is a Series A nuclear energy company founded by Robin Langtry and Brian Riordan that has raised $80M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 11 total peers—3 public (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private firms spanning the nuclear sector—including same-stage and adjacent-stage companies like Fuse Energy, Valar Atomics, Nano Nuclear Energy, Helion, and X-Energy.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression modeling, using the $80M total raised as a proxy for current value, applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-round transitions, implying a $160M valuation. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables yields a median valuation of $808M, derived from a tight peer set spanning $200M (Fuse Energy, Series A) to $6.0B (Valar Atomics, Series B), with Nano Nuclear Energy (Seed) at $808M.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $136M (low) to $929M (high), with a median of $484M. This wide band reflects material dispersion within the peer set and differing applicability across methods. Key uncertainties include stage-specific valuation step-up conventions in frontier nuclear (the 2.0x multiplier is illustrative), the appropriate weighting of seed-stage versus Series B comparables, and how technology maturity and regulatory pathway differentiate pricing within the sector.
